newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed may have peaked after soya gains.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed may have peaked after soya gains.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in Northern Europe have firmed along with the stronger dollar and strong soybean levels this week but nearing harvest pressure may reduce the price over the next few weeks, brokers said.
New crop buyers for ex-harvest rapeseed raised their offers by 2.50 marks on the week to 440 marks a tonne free Hamburg while sellers were cautious.
Rapeseed prices for delivery at points other than Hamburg were in a broadly steady 425-437.50 marks range for August and at 445 for Sept/Oct.
November rapeseed on the Matif futures traded at 457 marks, up one from Thursday's close and up 16 on the week.
Rapeseed harvesting was gathering pace across the country but efforts were disrupted in the north by frequent rainfall, which caused delays and drying costs.
The weather outlook for next week is sunny and dry, which should help speed harvesting and produce an overview over likely yields.
Latest area estimates, which were down from earlier estimates but still above last year, put winter rapeseed at 859,025 hectares (777,190 in 1996) and spring rapeseed at 56,988 ha (76,435 ha).
Yields achieved so far in the main growing region of Mecklenburg are up at 3.1 tonnes per hectare (tph) compared with 1.96 tph in Mecklenburg last year and the 1996 German average of 2.28 tph.
In the products, Aug/Oct rape meal was steady at 22.75-23.00 marks/100 kg and Nov/Jan slightly down at 24.25 (24.50).
Rape oil sellers prices were higher after the Rotterdam markets rose this week on soft oils buying as well as firmer international dollar and soy oil quotations.
Aug and Sept/Oct rape oils were each up 3.25 marks on the week at 95.00 and 96.25 marks respectively.
